Package neqsim.process.dynamics

Class EventScheduler

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.dynamics.EventScheduler
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class EventScheduler extends Object implements Serializable
Simple priority-queue-backed event scheduler for dynamic process simulations and safety studies.

Events are scheduled at absolute simulation time (seconds). At each integration step the caller invokes fireDueEvents(double) with the current simulation time; all events with time <= now are fired in time order and removed from the queue.

Typical use cases:

  • Initiating Operator Action (IOA) / Independent Operator Action (IOA) signals at a fixed post-trip time in safety studies.
  • ESD trip sequences (close-shut valve at t=2 s, depressurize at t=5 s).
  • Setpoint changes for controller tuning studies.

The scheduler itself is Serializable. It can therefore be serialized independently when every Runnable payload is also serializable. The scheduler attached to ProcessSystem is intentionally a transient runtime service and is not included automatically in a serialized process snapshot.

1.0

Even Solbraa

    • scheduleTransactionalEvent

      public EventScheduler.ScheduledEvent scheduleTransactionalEvent(double time, String label, Runnable action, String... transientStateIdentities)
      Schedules an event whose action declares every in-memory transient-state participant it may mutate.

      A ProcessSystem transaction accepts pending events only through this API and only when every declared identity belongs to a registered, completely covered participant. The declaration is a fail-closed orchestration contract: the action must not mutate undeclared objects, perform external I/O, publish externally visible events, or schedule an unscoped event. Those effects cannot be undone by participant snapshots.

      This method does not require the Runnable to be serializable for an in-memory transaction. Java checkpoint serialization still requires a serializable payload, exactly as for scheduleEvent(double, String, Runnable).

      Parameters:
      time - absolute simulation time in seconds
      label - short diagnostic label
      action - event payload
      transientStateIdentities - stable identities of every participant the action may mutate
      Returns:
      the scheduled transaction-scoped event
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the identity array is null, empty, contains null/empty identities, or contains duplicate identities

    • getNextEventTime

      public double getNextEventTime()
      Returns the earliest pending event time without mutating scheduler state.

      Adaptive/event-aware integrators can use this value to shorten a proposed timestep so an accepted physical step lands exactly on an event boundary rather than stepping past a trip, setpoint change, or operator action.

      Returns:
      earliest pending absolute event time in seconds, or positive infinity when no event is pending

    • getDueEvents

      public List<EventScheduler.ScheduledEvent> getDueEvents(double now)
      Returns pending events that are due at or before now without firing or removing them.

      The returned list is an immutable copy in scheduler order. This allows a transient transaction/event-localization layer to inspect an event boundary without changing pending/fired bookkeeping or executing event actions.

      Parameters:
      now - absolute simulation time in seconds
      Returns:
      immutable copy of due pending events

    • fireDueEvents

      public int fireDueEvents(double now)
      Fires all events with time <= now in time order.

      An event is removed from the pending queue and appended to the fired log only after its action completes successfully. If an action throws a RuntimeException, the failure is logged and rethrown immediately. The failing event remains pending, later due events are not executed, and the caller can abort the physical-step attempt instead of silently continuing after a failed trip, setpoint, or operator action.

      This fail-loud bookkeeping contract is not a whole-process transaction: an action that mutates external state and then throws may already have produced side effects. Qualified rejected-step execution must still restore every mutated object or defer side effects until step acceptance.

      Parameters:
      now - current simulation time in seconds
      Returns:
      number of events fired successfully in this call
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if a due event action fails

    • snapshot

      public EventScheduler.Snapshot snapshot()
      Captures the pending/fired scheduler bookkeeping for deterministic transient rollback.

      This operation does not execute, clone, or serialize event actions. The returned snapshot is independent of later queue/list changes because it copies both event lists.

      Returns:
      immutable scheduler bookkeeping snapshot

    • restore

      public void restore(EventScheduler.Snapshot snapshot)
      Restores pending/fired scheduler bookkeeping from a previous snapshot().

      Restoring membership does not reverse side effects from actions that have already executed. A rejected transient trial must not rely on this method alone when an event mutates external state.

      Parameters:
      snapshot - snapshot to restore
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if snapshot is null
